newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says too soon to tell if images spot sailor.
newsitem.headline: Canada says too soon to tell if images spot sailor.

text.p: Canadian authorities said on Monday it was too early to tell whether satellite images captured the boat of Canadian sailor Gerry Roufs, who is missing in remote South Pacific seas.

"At this point, we cannot say whether or not we have found something," said Ed Langham, a spokesman for Radarsat, a satellite program operated by a joint venture of Canadian federal and provincial governments and private business.
Canadian authorities were analyzing the radar satellite data to help in the search for Roufs, who is missing somewhere between New Zealand, South America and Antarcticas.
Roufs, a competitor in the Vendee Globe round-the-world sailing race, was last heard from last Tuesday about 2,175 miles 3,500 km from the southern tip of Chile.
On Sunday, a cargo ship and another race competitor looking for Roufs abandoned their search, but another cargo ship was reported heading to the area.

Langham said officials were analyzing data from a Radarsat microwave radar satellite that made two sweeps on Sunday and one on Monday of the region in which Roufs was lost. Radarsat was preparing for another satellite search of the area on Wednesday.

Langham told a news conference that the satellite could capture images through cloud or darkness and that under ideal conditions, like calm seas and low winds, it could easily pick up images of boats. As an example, he showed a satellite image of boats in Singapore harbor.

But seas between 12.5 and 18.6 feet (20 and 30 metres) and winds of up to 50 miles (80 km) were making the South Pacific satellite images much more difficult to decipher, he said. Officials expected to have more information on the satellite images later on Monday.

Roufs is missing in a region much less accessible by rescue aircraft than the area from which Australian forces rescued two other race competitors, Frenchman Thierry Dubois and Briton Tony Bullimore, whose boats had capsized.
